about: How people say how long ago they last saw someone, in passing: never a calendar date (owner, Oct 15, evening: nobody says a date in speech, 'I talked to Diana on November 13'). The first row whose upToDays covers the gap is said. Authored, calibrated to the way Americans mention a recent contact in the conversation bank; the engine only picks the row by the contact record's date. `gap` says how long that is as a greeting hears it (recent, a while, long: "I just saw you yesterday" only when recent), and `since` whether the words read after "since" ("since last week", never "since a few days ago"); both are marks a line may require.
author: Words line, Claude Sonnet 5.5
